title: License True-Up Charge on an ELA Renewed Under the New Terms
scenario_text:
Hydra Software licenses its platform through Enterprise License Agreements (ELAs) and reconciles over-deployment through an annual true-up governed by its Licensing Policy.

Version 1 (ELAs signed through 2023-12-31): "Annual true-up for deployments exceeding entitlement is billed at 100% of list price per additional unit, with no surcharge."

Version 2 (effective 2024-01-01): "Annual true-up is billed at 100% of list price per additional unit plus a 20% retroactive-use surcharge on units deployed beyond entitlement." v2 includes a transition clause: "An ELA signed before January 1, 2024 applies v1 true-up terms for its original term. Upon renewal of the ELA on or after January 1, 2024, all true-ups during the renewal term are governed by v2, including the 20% surcharge, regardless of the terms of the expiring agreement. Mid-term true-ups within the original term remain under v1."

The licensing operations record for customer Brightmoor Bank shows: original ELA O-772, Signed 2022-06-01, 2-year term; renewal ELA O-772-R, Signed 2024-06-01, 2-year renewal term (2024-06-01 through 2026-05-31). The 2025 annual true-up finds 40 units deployed beyond entitlement.

A licensing operations manager emails the account team on 2025-06-10: "Brightmoor's 2025 true-up is 40 units over. Their original ELA had no surcharge. Do we bill this renewal-term true-up with the 20% surcharge or under the old no-surcharge terms?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the licensing record, determine how the 2025 true-up should be billed.
question: How should the 2025 true-up for Brightmoor Bank be billed?
choices: Under v2: 100% of list price per over-deployed unit plus the 20% retroactive-use surcharge, because the ELA was renewed 2024-06-01 and all true-ups during the renewal term are governed by v2.
Under v1: 100% of list price with no surcharge, because the original ELA was signed 2022-06-01 under v1 and its terms carry through renewals.
No true-up is owed, because over-deployment true-ups applied only to the original term, not to renewal terms.
Under v2's surcharge only (the 20%), without the 100%-of-list base charge, because the base charge was grandfathered from v1.
